title: Muck Everyday Wash
meta_description: Muck Everyday Wash is a dog-shampoo advertisement built on a refusal: dogs are dogs, and they are allowed to smell like it.
role: Concept, art direction, generative production, edit
deck: A wash that argues against the entire category it sits in. Submitted to Filmsupply EditFest as an advertisement, and written as a manifesto.

proof.title: For dirty-free dogs.
proof.note: Every product in this category sells a dog that smells like dessert. Muck sells the mud instead, which means the packaging has to survive being photographed inside it.

shots.alt: The Muck Everyday Wash bottle photographed head-on inside a symmetrical crown of brown mud splashing outward against a black background.
shots.caption: Hero / impact

shots.alt: The same bottle half-buried at an angle in a shallow pool of mud, lit from above against black.
shots.caption: Hero / landing

shots.alt: A muddy dog's paw pressed against the mud-covered bottle as it tips over into a puddle.
shots.caption: Paw / endorsement

shots.alt: The bottle standing in mud with a set of wet paw prints running down the front label.
shots.caption: Label / paw prints

shots.alt: Front label of the bottle under thick mud, reading Everyday Wash, muck, and For dirty-free dogs with dirty-free struck through.
shots.caption: Front label

shots.alt: Back label of the bottle, mud-flecked, carrying the product copy and the line Tested on animals. They love it.
shots.caption: Back label

proof.caption: The bottle is never clean in a single frame, because a clean bottle would be selling the opposite product. Even the strikethrough is on the label: dirty-free is crossed out before the customer can ask for it.

acts.title: Dogs are dogs.
acts.note: The film is a list. It spends four lines naming what a dog is not, then gives the rest of its length to what a dog is.

items.title: Dogs are not
items.copy: Toys. Princes and princesses. Handbag dolls.

items.title: Dogs are dogs
items.copy: Let them roll in muck. Let them smell like true dogs.

pipeline.title: Pipeline.
pipeline.note: The manifesto was written first and everything else was cut to it, including the packaging.

items.label: Write
items.copy: The copy came first; the film was cut to the list rather than the other way round.

items.label: Generate
items.copy: Bottle, label, and mud states generated as one consistent product set.

items.label: Edit
items.copy: Cut for Filmsupply EditFest under the advertisement category.

items.label: Export
items.copy: Landscape master for the festival, packaging stills for the campaign board.
